changes.summary: Anthropic requests whose histories carry recognized nested tool_reference blocks are adapted to the template's support: rendered as text preserving names, order and IDs on templates without native reference expansion (the bundled Froggeric v22.5 template is unchanged), with native structured handling retained where supported. The reported 500 reproduction returns 200, ordinary prompt bytes are unchanged, and unsupported blocks keep the clean HTTP 400. The chat template, defaults, configuration and sampling behavior are unchanged.

Responses API: namespaced function and custom tools, inline additional_tools inventories, chronological replay/history and image-containing tool results map onto the chat path with one reversible, collision-safe identity shared by declarations, selected names, replay and full/SSE outputs. Namespaced members prefer the namespace__leaf identity; contested spellings escalate deterministically; unadvertised model names pass through. Malformed recognized replay and invalid named selections, namespaces and nested function-choice shapes are rejected with normal request errors before identity translation. Collision-retired identities bind as history-only: they stay distinct and cannot be called or required.

Qwen tool-argument parsing: anyOf/oneOf string unions keep objects and arrays when the parameter schema (in its own $id scope) accepts the decoded value, and declared type:string parameters keep explicit text including a literal null/NULL/Null. Existing coercion for nullable, nonstring, untyped and unknown parameters is unchanged.

Omitted non-Harmony Responses completion-token budgets defer to the existing scheduler bounds until after multimodal (image) input expansion, so image requests without an explicit limit stop failing the pre-expansion context check; explicit limits and Harmony are unchanged. Adapted from upstream PR 35524 (issue 29287).

Responses input items choose the open dict arm first, so a namespaced tool declaration, a replayed call and any newer wire field keep their namespace under pydantic 2.14.1 as well as 2.13.4; constructed SDK models still fall through to their own arm and malformed values still reach the normal /v1/responses request error instead of being silently dropped.

Registered container and cache tests: 52 passed, 1 skipped, and 1 existing fixture failure that reproduces identically on the base when the real native FlashInfer wins over the synthetic namespace, so this is recorded as a bounded known exception rather than an all-green run. Head ab3f41671c80dcf95febd210890b56c039bce2e0 on base 4d668a2d6b keeps the Responses input item on the open dict arm first, preserving namespaces, newer wire fields and supported SDK objects. 384 CPU tests with 303 subtests pass on both the previous pydantic 2.13.4/pydantic-core 2.46.4 pair and the accepted pydantic 2.14.1/pydantic-core 2.50.1 pair; the two runs overlap and are not summed, and this new evidence is separate from the dated 3a4de813 acceptance below. validation.correction_live: Recorded 2026-10-29. Local HTTP compatibility passed 5/5 against localhost fixtures before and after the aiohttp and yarl upgrade; no remote HTTP encoder was configured or exercised, and the separate profile path uses local A4000 preprocessing. Seven live API checks, the real uncoached Codex MCP execution and replay, and the image callback passed on the Flash-Next profile, which runs the corrected source with the adaptive width policy, medium reasoning effort and diagnostics off as an actual working service. The previously accepted two-profile qualification is reused as dated evidence; no additional 27B, performance, cache or NVMe campaign was run.
validation.container_cache: Recorded 2026-10-29 for PR #147 (head 22f5b99dc6b8350e2903375b0dcf7b41b7df4255 over original 059d3ab6fb163d55ffa6e3e95f8d98981b5a52e0, Penny and John authorship preserved, merged the same day). The compiled FlashInfer artifact is reused only when a fingerprint of the actual sources, toolchain shared libraries and ABI matches, with the one exception recorded below, and the small artifact travels through GHCR; changed, corrupt or unresolved inputs cannot reuse it. 66 tests with 4 subtests pass, with one optional probe skipped in the light test environment and passing separately inside the actual image. Local restore measured about 3 seconds; no full hosted build speedup is proved yet. The expectation that the first production build would compile and seed the cache was confirmed on 2026-10-29 by run 40885090275: the restore found no artifact, the module compiled, and the publish step seeded ghcr.io/jpezzulli/sglang-rtxpro6000:flashinfer-sm120-cache (index digest sha256:30eefe0801d1e572b52c90c0da9abda7fb9f0a28c458210ddb57274e37401301); the published image built from the previous source has no accepted input record. A confirmed follow-up review finding (2026-10-29, https://github.com/jpezzulli/sglang-rtxpro6000/pull/147#discussion_r4412613583) qualifies the reuse claim: the optional native `--build-cache` path can restore a previous binary without accounting for injected `NVCC_APPEND_FLAGS` or `NVCC_PREPEND_FLAGS`, confirmed on the existing CPU probe, so a native caller changing those flags may not rebuild; the automated container build defines or forwards neither variable and the rejected image's `Config.Env` carries neither, so the automated build is unaffected. The finding is triaged as non-blocking for the automated build, the native opt-in case is unresolved with no fix implemented and no deferral decision, and independent review is otherwise clean with no model performance improvement claimed. A cold restore on that first production build was the documented expectation and is what was observed, so it says nothing about later build times; no host-side parity, banner or GPU acceptance result for the new image is claimed here either.
exceptions: The versioned image is published; what is not claimed here is full model qualification, throughput or cache-restore timing, and the pennyroyal-v3.1.4 tag and GitHub release accompany this documentation change rather than being observed inside it.

Evidence runs are recorded separately and are not summed; the Flash-Next generation mismatches above are accepted limitations, not failures of the shipped fixes. The container cache work claims a faster local restore only, not measured hosted build time or model performance, and the native optional --build-cache NVCC flag limitation stays unresolved and non-blocking for the automated path.
